newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen hit by weak yen, JGB liquidation.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen hit by weak yen, JGB liquidation.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures slipped on Tuesday as the yen's drop against the dollar and sales of Japanese government bonds (JGBs) weighed on the market.
The market came under pressure early in the day on news Kabun Muto, director-general of Japan's Management and Coordination Agency, had urged the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to raise interest rates.
But players soon shrugged off the reports, choosing to focus instead on comments by BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka.
Both said the central bank's monetary policy would continue to be aimed at ensuring Japan's economic recovery.
"Matsushita and Mitsuzuka's comments implied the low interest environment would remain in Japan so that supported the market," said a trader with an Asian institution.
But the dollar's surge to fresh highs against the yen throughout the day weighed on Japanese interest rate and bond futures, he said.
The dollar was quoted at 126.22/32 after earlier hitting a four-and-a-half year peak of 126.52, its highest level since August 1992.
December Euroyen failed to climb above a technical barrier at 99.18, slipping back to 99.13 by 1120 GMT.
"December Euroyen should be supported around 99.12, but it will need to break above 99.18 before it can go to 99.20," the trader said.
June JGBs settled at 126.96 against their previous 127.17 after touching a record high of 127.33.
The trader said they could head lower to test support around 126.90 if the dollar continued to plough higher.
Eurodollar futures ended slightly firmer with September at 93.730 against its IMM close at 93.725 on volume of 4,500 lots.
